method: Live primary-source retrieval using Firecrawl targeted page reads; summaries inspected, claims limited to supported scope. Established frameworks are combined with original ClimbOS design recommendations and labeled hypothetical examples.

sources.title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice — The forecaster's toolbox / forecast accuracy
sources.claim_scope: Out-of-sample accuracy, simple forecasting benchmarks, temporal evaluation, and limitations of error metrics.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200; redirected to toolbox.html#sec-accuracy. Retrieved guidance distinguishes training and test evaluation, rolling forecasting origins, and scale-dependent and percentage errors. No publication date established.

sources.title: Google Analytics — Get started with attribution
sources.claim_scope: Attribution credit assignment, model-dependent reporting, and possible conversion-credit revisions.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200; current page describes available attribution models and conversion reattribution. Supports treating attribution settings and revisions explicitly; does not establish experimental causal lift for customers.

sources.title: Stripe — Usage-based pricing for SaaS: A guide
sources.claim_scope: Usage-based pricing mechanics, metering, predictability, billing surprise, hybrid packages, and usage transparency.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200 after search located canonical URL. Page describes consumption-based charges and risks of unpredictable bills and revenue. Used for model tradeoffs, not provider fees or optimal ClimbOS pricing.

sources.title: Stripe — CAC SaaS: A guide for businesses
sources.claim_scope: CAC numerator, acquired paying-customer denominator, and sales/marketing cost context.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200. Retrieved definition divides sales and marketing costs by new paying customers. Book does not adopt article's broad ratio benchmarks as universal operating thresholds.

sources.title: R stats — Power Calculations for Two-Sample Test for Proportions
sources.claim_scope: Reference implementation for proportion-test power calculations and parameter constraints.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200. Reference describes solving for one unspecified parameter and warns about impossible conditions and numerical root-finding limits. Book does not assert a particular ClimbOS sample-size implementation was tested.

sources.title: OpenAI — Evaluation best practices
sources.claim_scope: Task-specific representative evaluation, human calibration, comparison, and continuous evaluation.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200; current guide discusses nondeterminism, task-specific evaluation, grader bias, and avoiding unnecessary multi-agent complexity. Page also notes hosted Evals lifecycle dates. No model recommendation or price imported into the book.

sources.title: OpenAI — Structured model outputs
sources.claim_scope: Schema-based responses, supported schema behavior, refusals, and incomplete-output handling.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200. Guide documents JSON Schema adherence features and limitations. Book separates structural validity from truth and semantic validation; avoids copying volatile numeric schema limits.

sources.title: Convex — Actions
sources.claim_scope: External calls and side effects in actions; transactional boundaries and explicit failure handling.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200. Page describes actions, runtime restrictions, nonautomatic action retry, and database interactions. Book uses architectural implications rather than unneeded exact limits.

sources.title: Vercel — Function limits
sources.claim_scope: Plan-, runtime-, and feature-dependent execution constraints.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200. Targeted read reported last updated August 24, 2026. Book intentionally avoids fixed timeout or pricing tables and requires implementation-time verification.

sources.title: Resend — Idempotency keys
sources.claim_scope: Supported request deduplication and documented 24-hour idempotency-key retention.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200. Supports stable-key retries for supported endpoints within a limited retention window. Application outbox and longer-lived ledger are original ClimbOS design recommendations, not claims of indefinite provider deduplication.

sources.title: OpenAI — Safety in building agents
sources.claim_scope: Untrusted-input handling, prompt injection, data leakage, constrained data flow, and approval boundaries.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200. Page advises keeping untrusted variables outside developer messages and combining safeguards. Its builder is subject to lifecycle changes; book cites safety principles without recommending adoption of a retiring product.

sources.title: OpenAI — Data controls
sources.claim_scope: Feature-specific retention, storage, and data-control requirements.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200. Page distinguishes abuse monitoring, retention controls, and feature-specific conditions. Book makes no blanket zero-retention claim and requires endpoint-specific review.

sources.title: OpenAI — Deprecations
sources.claim_scope: Need to monitor current service/model lifecycle and hosted Evals/Agent Builder retirement notices.
sources.evidence_summary: HTTP 200. Retrieved notice includes products with October–November 2026 sunset timelines. Book directs implementers to verify dates and avoid new dependencies on retiring hosted evaluation or builder products.

limitations: Living documentation is mutable. Retrieval on the cutoff date does not establish its historical contents on another date.
Publication dates were not established; null means unknown, not equal to retrieval date. Vercel page's reported last-update date is distinguished from publication date.
The original guessed Stripe usage-pricing URL returned HTTP 404 and was replaced after search by the verified canonical URL. The failed URL is not used as support in final books.
Research used targeted retrieved answers rather than full-page archival copies. Claims were kept within inspected content; no exhaustive literature-review claim is made.
No live ClimbOS repository behavior, provider benchmark, market willingness to pay, advertising performance, or production deployment was verified by these books.
All worked business metrics, prices, fees, policy thresholds, and implementation outcomes are hypothetical unless separately attributed. No hypothetical values describe Formkit.
Current model identifiers and provider price tables are deliberately omitted; implementers must verify actual model availability, pricing, billing definitions, and SDK/runtime versions.
Search feedback was attempted once but the provider rejected it because its 120-second window had expired; no research result depended on feedback acceptance.
